chunks: From him, from Fazalat ibn Ayyub, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Baseer who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about wine being made into vinegar. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem if that which overwhelms it is not put into it.'

key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (specifically the drink that causes intoxication, often considered najasah)

ai.seo_question: Is wine considered pure when it turns into vinegar according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of *naskh* (transformation) in wine, specifying that the addition of external agents is permissible only if they do not overpower the natural fermentation process, thereby preserving the integrity of the transformation. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between natural change and artificial alteration, ensuring the resulting vinegar is distinct from the original wine. This ruling is foundational for understanding purity (*taharah*) and consumption (*halal*) of fermented products in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: From him, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the wine made into vinegar. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No problem if one does not make to be in it, what overwhelms it’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from abu Basir who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about wine which is turned into vinegar. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if one has not placed in it what overwhelms it.’”
